Subject: CMK delegation & transport questions

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement and security had a few follow-ups as we evaluate a private deployment: primarily around customer-managed keys (CMK) and the precise controls Redwood will assert over operator access and cross-region transport of telemetry/logs.

Two specific asks from our side:
1) If we choose BYOK (our CMK), can you confirm the exact responsibilities split (key provisioning, rotation, escrow, and emergency key-release)? We need language we can show our legal/regulatory team.
2) Will any telemetry or debug artifacts ever leave our VPC in unredacted form during breakglass investigations? If so, under what legal/contractual guardrails?

Procurement also asked for a draft DPA and any sample redlines you typically accept for private deployments. Can you attach those?

Appreciate a one-page summary of options and the recommended default for regulated customers.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Security Operations Lead
Caldera Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Mar 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CMK delegation & transport questions

Alex — thanks, and great questions. I pulled together a concise set of options and attached a draft DPA + our operator access matrix. High level:

Option A — Hosted (not applicable if you need private).

Option B — Private (VPC) with Redwood-managed keys: Redwood provisions KEKs in our KMS; we manage rotation and backups. We provide audit logs and a key-wrapping model; Redwood never stores application plaintext. Operator access is strictly scoped to tooling telemetry and metrics; engineers do NOT have default decryption capability. Breakglass is possible but must be gated (see operator matrix).

Option C — Private BYOK (recommended for regulated PHI workflows): Customer supplies CMK (you control the key material). Responsibilities: provisioning and rotation remain with Caldera unless you request Redwood to manage rotation as an administrative service (requires explicit SOW).
- Escrow: We do not require escrow for normal BYOK. If Caldera requests escrow for business continuity, we can accept a certified escrow agent under mutually agreed terms — escrow release requires multi-party approval (Caldera legal + Redwood compliance).
- Emergency release: We will only accept a documented, auditable release process. We will not assert unilateral access.

Telemetry & debug artifacts:
- Normal telemetry (metrics, anonymized traces) is routed out of the VPC to our monitoring and is redacted of customer payloads by default.
- Forensic artifacts for breakglass: collection requires a signed request, showing legal basis and JIT access approval. When permissible, artifacts can be moved to a secure Redwood incident bucket for analysis but will be encrypted with either your CMK or a temporary RW-key that we register. All transfers are logged and available to Caldera.

Next steps attached: redwood_private_dpa_draft.pdf (DPA + BYOK clauses) and operator_access_matrix.xlsx (operator roles, JIT controls, evidence types).

Please review and flag any redlines. Happy to hop on a short call with your privacy team this week to walk through the escrow wording.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Security & Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_private_dpa_draft.pdf, operator_access_matrix.xlsx

Also: operator access matrix needs a clear sentence that we do NOT have plaintext access to application payloads when BYOK is used (important; legal will push).

I can take the customer call if needed; want to keep it tight and not open to long back-and-forths.

2) Operator access: explicit "no-plaintext" statement when BYOK is selected, plus JIT breakglass flow that records approver identity, time, and scope.
3) Telemetry transport: clarified that forensic artifacts transferred for incident response will be encrypted with your CMK (preferred) or a transient RW-key wrapped under your CMK; we will provide logs and access records to Caldera for audit.
